description.value: The study examined resting-state functional connectivity of bilateral habenula regions in autistic and neurotypical participants, including group differences, developmental age-related variability, functional decoding, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

design.value: Retrospective multisite resting-state functional MRI study using participants selected from the ABIDE I and II datasets. Participant-level habenula-to-whole-brain correlation maps were compared between ASD and neurotypical groups and regressed on age and phenotypic measures.

description.value: The BRIEF GEC T-score measures executive function by compiling scores from composite indexes testing behavior regulation, emotional recognition, and cognitive regulation.
The DLS domain measured adaptive behavior encompassing everyday tasks necessary for independent living, including personal care, household responsibilities, and community activities.
Participants with autism spectrum disorder diagnoses made according to DSM-IV and DSM-5.

task_description.value: Resting state functional MRI data were used to calculate bilateral habenula whole-brain functional connectivity.

description.value: Resting state functional MRI data were acquired across 24 scanning sites.
For all participants, a T1-weighted structural image was collected and used for registration to Montreal Neurological Institute space.

Data were preprocessed using fMRIPrep 23.1.3. Anatomical images were intensity-corrected, skull-stripped, segmented, and spatially normalized to MNI152 space; manual and automated quality control were performed; participants, sessions, or runs with excessive motion or fewer than 100 usable time points were removed; remaining data were denoised using AFNI’s 3dTproject.

steps.value: removed participants, sessions, or runs with framewise displacement greater than 0.35mm or fewer than 100 usable time points following motion censoring

model_settings.value: Averaged ROI time series were entered into a general linear model to generate whole-brain correlation maps for each participant. Fisher r-to-z transformed correlation maps were entered into group-level regression models with diagnosis as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site; AFNI’s 3dLMEr was used.

Phenotypic main effects among ASD participants and phenotypic interactions between ASD and NT groups were tested using group as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate at p < 0.05.
